title: Synchronized embedded desingularization with intrinsic ambient comparison
statement:
Work over $\mathbf Q$. Consider all closed immersions $X\hookrightarrow P$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $X$ reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and $P$ a smooth separated finite-type scheme, including finite disjoint unions of such pairs [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There exists an embedded resolution algorithm $E$ with a common totally ordered set of synchronization labels. It assigns to each pair a finite ordinary blowup tower $P_r\to\cdots\to P_0=P$ [def-nagata-global-blowup], retaining its centers $C_i\hookrightarrow P_i$, and the successive scheme-theoretic strict transforms $X_i\hookrightarrow P_i$ [def-nagata-strict-transform]. Each $C_i$ is contained in $X_i$, is nonempty, regular, and nowhere dense in $X_i$, and has coherent ideal on $P_i$ and on $X_i$ [pqf-def-coherent]; $X_r$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The tower is stopped when $X_i$ is regular; no subsequent exceptional-divisor cleanup is included. A closed subscheme is nowhere dense if its underlying closed set contains no nonempty open subset of the ambient scheme in question. Each stage has a distinct label, and the labels occur in the common prescribed order. The empty input and a regular $X$ have the empty tower.

For every smooth morphism $v:Q\to P$ between the indicated ambient schemes, the algorithm on $X\times_P Q\hookrightarrow Q$ is the pullback of the embedded tower, deleting precisely empty centers and retaining their labels; identities and compositions give the same labeled comparisons. No constant relative dimension is required. A label absent from a restricted tower denotes an empty center and an identity stage.

If the same reduced $X$ is closed embedded in two such ambient schemes, the two labeled towers of strict transforms of $X$, together with their ideal centers on those strict transforms, are canonically identified over $X$, with exactly the same labels. These intrinsic comparisons also respect isomorphisms of $X$ and are transitive for three embeddings. Here labels encode the invariant synchronization, not consecutive stage numbers renumbered independently on each component or open subset.

source.place: Expose VIII 2.3.11 and 2.3.13, printed pp.93--94: the strong Bierstone--Milman algorithm and the invariant synchronization correction of Bierstone--Milman--Temkin, Q-universal desingularization (2011), Theorem 6.1, Addendum and section 6.3. This embedded, labeled input is stated separately; the detailed reference is WANTED, not claimed to have been read. No Stacks tag supplies embedded resolution.

proof.text: Choose the simultaneous invariant calculus supplied by [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-resolution-invariant-calculus], and call its entire value set, including its least element, $V$. Fix this SAME calculus for every embedded pair. Its clauses (1)--(4) satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-trf-maximum-history-finite-realization]. For each pair $A$, set $E(A)=T_\nu(A)$ to its maximum-center realization. This supplies the finite ordinary embedded tower, all center conditions, regular final transform, and common label set $L=(V\setminus\{\bot\})^{\mathrm{op}}$. It stops at first regularity, gives empty towers for empty or regular inputs, and takes maxima over entire finite disjoint unions. Retain its center ideals and lower-cut diagrams. The lemma determines this realization up to the canonical blowup identifications; Steps 2--3 compare these very realizations, rather than choosing independent algorithms on different pairs.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11, printed p.93 (stop before exceptional-divisor cleanup), and 2.3.13, p.94 (common invariant synchronization); old Steps 1--2.

proof.text: For a smooth ambient map $v:Q\to P$, take the Step 1 histories on $A=(X\hookrightarrow P)$ and $B=(X\times_PQ\hookrightarrow Q)$ with their specified initial cartesian identification. Both use the fixed calculus, start empty, and stop at first regularity, as required by [lem-trf-maximum-history-smooth-deletion]. Its comparison is cartesian on ambient schemes and scheme-theoretic strict transforms, extends center ideals, and deletes precisely empty centers while retaining labels, for arbitrary relative dimensions. Its final-bottom assertion rules out additional stages over $Q$. For composable smooth ambient maps, all three Step 1 histories use this same calculus, so the lemma's identity and composition laws apply to these particular comparisons and their lower-cut diagrams, including identity stages at absent labels.

source.place: VIII 2.3.4--2.3.5, printed pp.91--92 (contracted pullback and synchronization), and 2.3.13, p.94 (arbitrary smooth morphisms); old Steps 3--4 and 6.

proof.text: For two embeddings of the same $X$, the identity $\operatorname{id}_X$ identifies their initial strict transforms; their empty histories have no earlier center ideals to match. Apply [lem-trf-maximum-history-intrinsic-cocycle] to their Step 1 histories and this initial identity. This identifies their strict-transform diagrams and ideal centers with exactly the same active labels. Apply its general isomorphism case for functoriality in $X$ and its composition law for three embeddings. Its compatibility with restriction and smooth pullback gives the corresponding compatibility of these intrinsic comparisons. Together with Step 2 these towers and comparisons are the asserted assignment.
